about: Skill-routing holdout set, version 3: the same 15 skills. M skills: 1 positive (expects load) + 1 negative. U skills: 2 prose positives (expects recommend) + 1 hard negative. Not tuned against; run it only to report. tests/learn/trigger-prompts.test.ts holds the split and the leakage guard.

cases.prompt: Kick off /ak:super-align for the idea of letting customers export their dashboards. Nobody agrees yet on formats or who gets access.
We haven't settled whether the new importer should dedupe records or just flag them. Can you lay out the options and pick one?
Rename the `usr` variable to `user` in src/session.ts; nothing else.
Run /ak:super-bound now: we agreed to move sessions from cookies to server-side storage and I want the implementation plan and tickets.
We signed off on replacing the cron scheduler with a queue. Write up the spec and break it into work items.
Bump the lodash version in package.json to the latest patch release.
Go ahead with /ak:super-ship for the rate limiter branch, dry run only, nothing leaves this machine.
Everything on feature/rate-limit is approved. Check it for leaked secrets, commit, and open the pull request.
What does `git push --force-with-lease` protect against?
Take a hard look at the changes in src/billing before I open the PR. Anything that would get rejected?
What is a CODEOWNERS file for?
Invoke /ak:compound for the reviewer's catch about unbounded retries; I want it kept as a lesson.
We finally figured out why the webhook signature check failed in staging. Save what we learned somewhere the team will find it.
What's a good template for a bug report?
Kick off /ak:compound-refresh. Two of our notes about caching now say opposite things.
Our written guidance on error handling has drifted and some entries clash. Can you reconcile them?
How often should a team revisit its coding guidelines, as a rule of thumb?
Invoke /ak:receiving-review for pull request 77. Some of the suggestions look wrong to me.
The bot left twenty suggestions on my PR. Apply the good ones and reply to the rest.
What does 'nit:' mean at the start of a review comment?
Invoke /ak:babysit-pr for pull request 88 until the checks settle.
My PR keeps going red whenever main moves. Stay on it and react when something new happens.

Kick off /ak:ultraqa on the file upload endpoint in the local build.
Try to break the new import command with weird inputs and tell me what crashes.
What's the difference between fuzzing and property-based testing?
Invoke /ak:wayfind for the observability overhaul. We don't know the path yet.
Moving everything onto the new event bus is full of unknowns. List the big open decisions for me.
Give me a one-paragraph definition of technical debt.
I'm landing cold in this repo. Survey the storage layer and list what you verified and what you could not.
Rename the config loader's search path variable everywhere it's used.
Implement the approved change to the rate limiter; write the failing test before the code.
Here's a rough idea about caching that nobody has looked at yet. Should we even do it?
Show me a matrix of acceptance criteria against the commands that prove them on this commit.
Two of the acceptance checks fail on this branch. Change the code until they pass.
Is this requirements doc coherent enough to plan from? Point out ambiguity.
Look through the diff in src/api for bugs.
Search got about three times slower after last week's deploy and nobody knows why. Track it down.
It's basically a bug that the app has no dark mode. Add one.
